name: wag1
label: WhatsApp Guard
description: A watchtower for the WhatsApp bridge: unread chats and message counts, the chats that need attention, a merged live feed of the newest messages, a watchlist that raises a banner when a named person or number writes, and how much the bridge answered on its own in the last 24 hours. Everything is read from the bridge's own database through the WhatsApp module - nothing is simulated and nothing is stored here except the watchlist.

steps: Open Apps > WhatsApp Guard. Every panel comes from GET /api/modules/whatsapp/{status,chats,auto-contacts,messages}: the bridge's SQLite database, not a simulation. Unread chats and messages come from the chat list, the feed is the newest messages across the eight busiest chats, and auto-sent 24h / drafts waiting come from the same figures Settings > Auto reply shows. It refreshes every 15 seconds and pauses while the tab is hidden; the pause button stops it entirely.

Use the search box in the Watchlist card: it filters the bridge's chats by name or number as you type, and clicking a result watches that chat (Enter watches the first match). You can also click any row in 'Needs attention' or 'Chats' - a star means it is already watched, and clicking again stops watching. An unread message from a watched chat raises the red banner at the top with how many are waiting. A chat is watched by its id, so renaming a contact does not silently unwatch it. The list lives in this browser (localStorage, key wag1_watch), so it is per machine; the conversation and the auto-reply settings are untouched.

Unread counts are the bridge's own unread column, not a recount, so they clear when the chat is read (in WhatsApp or with the module's markread). Auto-sent 24h counts only replies the bridge actually sent, not drafts it offered and you discarded.

Pulse has three: the donut is messages in vs out over 24 hours (the same auto-contacts figures Settings > Auto reply shows), the bars are unread by chat (the six worst), and the sparkline is unread as this page has seen it since it opened - one point per 15-second poll, kept in memory, not a history from the bridge. Numbers count up rather than jumping, a message that arrives while you are looking flashes in the feed, and the dot beside 'updated' pulses when something new landed. prefers-reduced-motion turns all of it off.
fixes: The header says unreachable or the panels are red
The WhatsApp bridge is not answering: open Apps > WhatsApp and check its status/QR first. The page shows the module's error instead of pretending there is no data.
A chat is read in WhatsApp but still shows unread here

The bridge refreshes its unread column from the phone's own messages; press refresh after the app has caught up. If it stays stuck, the module's repair (POST /api/modules/whatsapp/repair) rescans the stored history.

Chats you add by clicking (search result or row) are watched by id, so they match exactly. An entry typed as free text, or added before this change, matches the chat's name or id by substring, case-insensitive - a nickname WhatsApp does not have will not match. Remove the chip and add the chat by clicking it.
The feed reads the eight most recently active chats. A brand-new bridge with no synced history has nothing to show; sync history from the WhatsApp page first.
The sparkline is flat or empty

It is this page's own observation, not stored history: it starts when you open the page and keeps 40 points (about ten minutes). A flat line means the unread total did not change while you watched - the honest answer, not a fault. Reopen the page and it starts again.
The donut says 0 but there are messages
It counts the last 24 hours, and only chats in the auto-reply scope (the ones Settings > Auto reply lists). A quiet day really is 0; older traffic is not shown.
